adaptation: EGSQUAL is a survey scale for measuring perceived service quality of governmental WEBSITES. It was not designed to classify free-text feedback or mobile-app reviews.

This prototype uses service-quality dimensions as a qualitative coding frame: each issue extracted from an Arabic review is assigned one operational category, which carries a provisional EGSQUAL dimension.
The operational categories come from E-S-QUAL / E-RecS-QUAL and e-GovQual, which describe failure-oriented aspects (availability, fulfilment, responsiveness) that app reviews mention often.
An 'Unclear / Unmapped' category is used when the evidence does not show which aspect of the service failed.
limitations: The dimension definitions and the crosswalk are unverified until the full paper is read.
Two EGSQUAL dimensions (interactivity and personalization; aesthetics) have no operational category yet, so feedback about them is classified under the nearest category (usually Efficiency).
EGSQUAL was validated for websites; mobile apps add issues (crashes, updates, device compatibility) that the scale may not cover.
Short, dialectal Arabic reviews often lack enough detail to identify a dimension, hence the Unmapped category.
No inter-annotator agreement has yet been measured for the dimension coding.
